subject: Post-demo: ACME integration & prompt-governance next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Great call — next steps: SDK auth, routing, prompt governance

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Really helpful to see the ACME use cases (support triage + knowledge augmentation + policy-compliance assistant). Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the short list of next steps and a proposed owner for each so we can keep momentum: 

1) Technical deep-dive (SDK + auth): Rishi to run a 60-min session with Alex/eng to walk SDK install, API keys vs OIDC flow, and example code for structured output.
   - Owner: Rishi Malhotra (SE)
   - Suggested window: Wed 5/6 or Thu 5/7

2) Routing & model selection: confirm latency vs cost targets so we can recommend routing (hosted -> dedicated fallback / region pinning) and quantization profiles.
   - Owner: Marissa

3) Embeddings & reranker proof-of-concept: provide sample pipeline (indexing cadence, vector dimensionality, reranker scoring) and benchmark targets.
   - Owner: Rishi

4) Prompt templates & governance: share our prompt-versioning checklist and red-team plan for prompt-injection mitigations. ACME asked about versioning and auditability for system prompts; attached is a starting checklist.
   - Owner: Marissa + ACME security

Attachments: redwood-quickstart.pdf (SDK quickstart + auth patterns), prompt-governance-checklist.xlsx (prompt versioning + red-team playbook stub).

Quick asks from our side: could you confirm who on your eng/security side will join the technical session (name + email)? Also please share any latency SLOs for the support use case (p95 token latency target) so we can size routing options.

Thanks — I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme.com>

Marissa / Rishi — quick notes from an engineer's perspective ahead of Thu's session: 
- OIDC preferred. We run HashiVault + Okta; ideally the flow is: ACME IdP -> short-lived token -> Redwood private agent exchanges -> inference session. Need to understand if token exchange can be automated in the SDK.
- For deterministic structured output, JSON Schema or typed protobufs work best for us. If Redwood can emit validated JSON per response (with a schema name/version), that solves a lot of plumbing.
- On reranker cadence: we reindex nightly and run a lightweight rerank at query time. Curious about memory/latency trade-offs for a 25M doc index.

Looking forward to the session — will join Thu 5/7 10:00 PT.

Alex
Senior Engineer, Integrations | Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great call — next steps: SDK auth, routing, prompt governance

Thanks for the clarifying notes — below are concrete answers and what I'll cover in the deep-dive (Thu 5/7 10:00 PT):

1) Auth patterns (what we'll demo)
- OIDC token exchange: our SDK supports an OIDC flow via short-lived bearer tokens. Patterns: (a) direct OIDC token in hosted/private agent connector, (b) token-exchange via a small Redwood sidecar that swaps IdP token for a short-lived inference token. We'll demo both flows and include an example using Okta + Vault.
- API keys + rotation: supported for quick POCs, but for production we recommend OIDC with automated rotation for audit logs.

2) SDK setup + structured output
- We'll show the Node + Python SDK installs and a sample call returning typed JSON (schema name: support_incident.v1). The SDK has validation hooks; we also support function/tool-calling style responses that map directly to ticket creation. Example payloads and a sample JSON Schema will be in the repo link I share during the session.

3) Routing & model selection
- Recommendation based on your p95 latency target: if <200ms p95 use Dedicated or region-pin hosted with GPU selection; if 200-500ms p95 we can run hosted with aggressive prefix caching + KV cache. We'll bring a cost/latency tradeoff table. Also discuss automatic fallback policy (hosted -> dedicated-burst -> lower-parameter model) for graceful degradation.

4) Embeddings + reranker guidance
- For ~25M small docs: hybrid approach — store dense vectors in FAISS + shard by namespace, nightly reindex, ephemeral in-memory reranker for top-K. We suggest 128- to 512-d vectors depending on quality needs; default 384-d for a balance. We'll provide expected throughput numbers and a suggested batching config.

5) Prompt templates, governance & red-teaming
- Versioning: store prompt templates with a semantic version (major.minor.patch) and immutable system-prompts per model-version. Each deployment records the prompt-version in the inference audit log.
- Injection mitigations: escape/untrusted-input boundaries, response schema validators (reject non-conforming JSON), and allowlist models for system instructions. We recommend a pre-deploy static analyzer for prompt patterns and runtime detectors for anomalous tokens.
- Red-team: run scheduled adversarial tests (prompt injections + data-exfil attempts) and keep a triage board for regressions. We'll share a starter red-team prompt suite in the checklist.

Attachments I'll share during the session: a sample JSON Schema for support_incident.v1 and a reranker benchmarking doc. For now I've attached the two brief artifacts Marissa shared to this thread so you have them locally.

See you Thu — I'll send the calendar invite in a few minutes.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
